items.title: Mac and storage
items.explanation: The physical and logical places where software and its data live. This context keeps a file or process tied to the Mac and storage volume that actually contains it.
items.question: Where does this exist?

items.title: Installation and identity
items.detail: Where it came from and who made it
items.explanation: Provenance distinguishes a web download from an App Store or package-manager install, and identity records evidence such as signing and package receipts.
items.question: How did it get here, and can I identify it?
items.examples: Web · App Store · Homebrew · npm · developer signature

items.title: Software
items.explanation: The recognizable thing you chose to install, plus supporting packages or services. HAL uses this as the main point of entry instead of making you begin with low-level files.
items.question: What did I install?

items.title: Runtime
items.explanation: Runtime entities represent active work happening now or during an observed period. Installed software can exist without running, and one application may create many processes.
items.question: What is running?

items.title: Persistence
items.explanation: Persistence is separate from runtime. It records mechanisms that can launch software after login, restart it after reboot, or keep a helper available even when the main application is closed.
items.question: Why can this start or return automatically?
items.examples: Login item · LaunchAgent · LaunchDaemon · background helper · extension

items.title: Data
items.explanation: HAL separates valuable user work and configuration from disposable caches and logs. Ownership can be shared or uncertain, and uncertainty remains visible.
items.question: What does it leave behind, and is any of it reclaimable?
items.examples: Documents · settings · cache · logs · shared data

items.title: Resources
items.explanation: Resource observations describe changing system capacity. They are measurements over time, not permanent properties of an application.
items.question: What impact is it having right now or over time?

items.title: Events and incidents
items.explanation: Events form the timeline. Incidents mark a period where something became unhealthy or surprising. Their proximity to another event is evidence to investigate, not automatic proof of cause.
items.question: What happened, and when did it become a problem?
items.examples: Launch · update · file growth · memory-pressure incident

items.title: Relationships and evidence
items.detail: How HAL connects facts, with confidence
items.explanation: HAL links entities using observed facts and labeled inferences. Every inferred relationship should expose its supporting evidence and confidence so ambiguity remains visible.
items.question: How do we know these things belong together?
items.examples: Owns · launches · reads and writes · observed · inferred · confidence

items.title: Findings and alerts
items.explanation: HAL turns related observations into reviewable findings. A finding states its evidence and confidence; it does not silently convert correlation into certainty.
items.question: What deserves my attention?

items.title: Decisions and safe actions
items.detail: What you choose to do next
items.explanation: The final layer is human control: inspect, keep, dismiss, or explicitly approve a safe action. Phase 0 demonstrates this model with synthetic data and performs no cleanup.
items.question: What can I safely decide or do?
